A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UGround and SeeAct-V. Their main text, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original grounding and agent evaluations on six benchmarks, together with error analysis, data scaling experiments, and training-data ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds backbone, image-resolution, and referring-expression ablations in Appendix C, plus dataset analyses in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The principal architecture, training stages, and inference procedure remain unchanged. However, v1 Appendix C.1 explicitly describes injecting incorrect positional descriptions during data synthesis; v2 Appendix E.1 omits this step without explaining whether it was discontinued or merely removed from the documentation. An actual synthesis-method change therefore remains uncertain.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training-data sources and six evaluation benchmarks spanning web, mobile, and desktop interfaces. The new ablations reuse ScreenSpot's existing standard and agent settings; they introduce no additional dataset, task, or environmental coverage.

E2.justification: Table C.1 adds Qwen-VL-Chat without continual fine-tuning and the UGround-Qwen variant to comparisons with SeeClick and UGround. Comparator membership in the original benchmark tables is unchanged, including CogAgent in Table 2.

E3.justification: The main benchmark protocols remain stable. Appendix C adds controlled configurations: Qwen-based training with at most 30 elements per page, three fixed image resolutions versus dynamic resolution, and positional-RE removal while holding element counts constant. The stated long-page sampling also changes from a viewport block to up to three blocks; this does not establish that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v1 analyzes data scaling, data sources, and agent errors. v2 substantially extends this evidence with comparisons separating backbone and training-data contributions, fixed versus dynamic resolution tests, and positional-RE ablations under both ScreenSpot settings (Tables C.1-C.4). Tables E.1-E.3 additionally characterize training-data composition.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the evaluations. The new ablation tables retain point-estimate reporting; dataset-composition percentages do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Main-text Tables 2-9 retain their numerical results. New appendix results include 14.5% for Qwen-VL-Chat and 62.4% for UGround-Qwen in Table C.1, and fixed-resolution averages of 72.2%, 73.8%, and 73.2% in Table C.2. Table C.4 reports 64.9% without positional REs versus 68.8% with them for Web-Hybrid-only training. These are additional configuration comparisons, not performance improvements between versions. Dataset-composition results are also added.

T1.justification: Neither version supplies formal theoretical results or proofs. The new modularity argument and explanations of resolution and positional context are conceptual interpretations, not mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The introduction now explicitly includes releasing the grounding dataset among the contributions, whereas v1 explicitly promised model release. The central scientific claims remain the same: universal visual grounding, gains of up to approximately 20 percentage points, and competitive vision-only agents across six benchmarks.

C2.justification: New Appendix B argues that environmental complexity and idiosyncratic semantics motivate modular agents over monolithic models. Appendix C adds interpretations concerning data versus backbone contributions, dynamic resolution, and positional context, and explains why visual and functional REs are difficult to ablate separately. These substantially extend v1's interpretations, while its principal long-tail and desktop-data limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly states dataset release, adds academic-use and moderation information, reports approximately 700K source URLs, and documents the new ablation configurations. Conversely, it removes the positional-noise augmentation description and OmniACT's MiniLM-L12-H384 retrieval specification and detailed scoring explanation. Core hardware, training times, batch sizes, model endpoints, and planner prompts are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to ScreenAgent, Ferret-UI 2, and MM1.5, removes the MiniLM citation, and expands modular-agent positioning and the explicit novelty claim for its RE taxonomy. The principal relationship to SeeClick and CogAgent remains. Numerous other reference edits are publication updates or duplicate consolidation rather than changes in cited work.

P1.justification: v2 adds an ethics statement and dedicated philosophy and ablation appendices, updates cross-references, and copyedits prose, particularly the data-construction description. The main narrative, section order, and most existing explanations remain intact; much of the added text accompanies new scientific content.

P2.justification: The appendix substantially expands its quantitative displays with ablation Tables C.1-C.4 and composition Tables E.1-E.3. Figure D.4 replaces the Web-Hybrid example panel, the earlier appendix's arrow-annotation illustration is removed, and prompt tables gain clearer internal divisions. Existing benchmark tables and principal plots are retained, with appendix labels and placement updated.

improvement.justification: Appendix C provides useful additional tests of the data, backbone, resolution, and positional-RE choices, strengthening support for the existing central results. Dataset-composition tables also improve transparency. These benefits outweigh the limited documentation losses, but removal of positional-noise and OmniACT retrieval/scoring details weakens reproducibility, and the new comparisons still lack uncertainty reporting. The net improvement is supported but limited.
